goal: Introduce a shared, generic acars_messages store — one new SQLite table in src/db/schema.ts, a domain db module src/db/acarsMessages.ts, a pure src/acars.ts (canned set + validators), and a src/routes/acars.ts router mounted in src/server.ts — that becomes the substrate for datalink-style messages tied to a flight: uplink ('dispatch') and downlink ('cockpit') entries across categories (pdc, wx, freetext, position-report, dispatch, and whatever the sibling stories need). Ship one web-client page (client/ only) that renders a flight's thread newest-first with direction and category visibly distinguishable, and can send one of three canned free-text messages, which appears in the thread with no page reload. The schema and API are frozen this run so acars_pdc_request.md, acars_weather_request.md, acars_position_reports.md and acars_dispatch_loadsheet.md can write into them later without a migration.
frozen_decisions: AC1 (story, verbatim): Messages persist across server restarts and are scoped to the correct flight/leg.
AC2 (story, verbatim): The thread renders in chronological order with direction and category visibly distinguishable.
AC3 (story, verbatim): Sending a canned message creates a downlink entry visible without a page reload.
AC4 (story, verbatim): The data model is generic enough that the PDC and weather-request stories in this directory can write into it without a schema change.

Web client only. The Tauri/MCDU desktop client moved to oshogun/msfslogger_mcdu and is not in this tree; no MCDU code is touched and no MCDU-specific affordance (unread badge on the MCDU host) is built this run.

'Flight/leg id' in the story resolves to flights.id (the existing flights table, src/db/flights.ts + src/db/schema.ts), NOT planned_legs. The exact FK shape — nullability, ON DELETE, and whether an additional planned_leg reference column ships now for the pre-departure dispatch/PDC case — is the Designer's to resolve in T-001, not the Planner's and not an implementer's.
Canned outgoing messages are a fixed, hardcoded list for this run: 'WX REQUEST', 'GATE REQUEST', 'REQUEST PUSHBACK'. No admin UI, no free-typing.
None of the sibling ACARS stories (pdc, wx, position-report, dispatch loadsheet) is implemented this run. Their only claim on this run is AC4: the frozen schema must absorb them with no ALTER TABLE.
A Design step is mandatory and gates every implementation task: this run freezes a schema and an API contract that four later stories build on.
Never touch the user's running server on port 3000 or the live flights.db. Anything needing a live server runs on PORT=3100 in a scratch cwd against a copied flights.db (+ -wal, -shm).
Scratch servers are stopped by their recorded PID only. Never pkill by name or -f pattern.
Node 20 via nvm for every command: export NVM_DIR="$HOME/.nvm"; . "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh"; nvm use 20
No task straddles backend and frontend. Backend owns src/** and tests/**; frontend owns client/**.

This project has no unit coverage for src/db/** or src/routes/**, and this run does not build one. Pure logic (validators, the canned set, any ordering/formatting helper) gets Vitest coverage in tests/acars.test.ts; the db and route layers are verified manually against a scratch server, per .claude/ENVIRONMENT.md.
sequencing_rationale: Design is T-001 and gates everything, because the deciding questions are all schema questions that are expensive to revisit: whether category is a CHECK constraint or open TEXT (the position-report story wants an 'oooi' category the story's own five do not contain — a CHECK would make that a migration and break AC4), whether a request/reply correlation column ships now (wx and loadsheet are request/reply pairs), whether a dedup key ships now (PDC must return an identical clearance on re-request), whether a structured payload column ships now (loadsheet fixed fields, position lat/lon/alt), and whether a message can exist before its flights row does (PDC and dispatch happen before pushback, and startFlight() does not insert a flights row until the flight begins — src/flightManager.ts:236). Every one of those is cheap now and an ALTER TABLE later.

Phase 1 ships the substrate end to end at the API: table, db module, pure module, routes, mounted. It is independently falsifiable — a thread survives a server restart (AC1) and the four sibling-story message shapes insert and list with PRAGMA table_info unchanged (AC4) — and it isolates the run's only schema change behind its own reviewer gate before any client code exists.

Phase 2 ships what the user sees: the page, the ordering and the direction/category distinction (AC2), and the canned send that lands in the thread without a reload (AC3), on top of an API already proven durable.

The backend is ONE task, not four. src/db/schema.ts, src/db/acarsMessages.ts, src/acars.ts, src/routes/acars.ts and src/server.ts are one dependency chain on one owner with one verification session (scratch server + curl); splitting them would buy a diagram and cost three cold spawns that each re-read the same design sections.

The risky, story-defining part is isolated into a pure module: src/acars.ts takes no db, no express, no fs, no network, so direction/category/body validation and the canned set are falsifiable by npm test with no server at all, and the same module is what the sibling stories will import.

The client gets a dedicated page at /flight/:id/acars rather than a section inside FlightDetail.tsx. FlightDetail.tsx is already 473 lines and is a logbook summary (stats, map, altitude profile, export, delete); the four sibling stories all add ACTIONS to this surface (REQUEST CLEARANCE, REQUEST WX, REQUEST LOADSHEET), which would keep growing a page that has nothing else to do with datalink. A route also mirrors the datalink page the MCDU client will later consume from its own repo. FlightDetail.tsx gains only an entry-point link, and that link plus the page plus the route are one frontend task because they must land together.
src/server.ts and client/src/types.ts are each touched by exactly one task, so no path is shared inside a phase, and the two phases are separated by the T-003 reviewer gate anyway.

T-003 carries model_hint opus: it reviews the run's only schema change and the contract four later stories inherit. T-005 reviews a read/write page against a frozen API and stays at the reviewer default.
No DevOps task: no new dependency, no build, packaging or deploy change. The run is a table, a router and a page.

tasks.title: Freeze the acars_messages schema and the ACARS API contract
tasks.goal: Write .claude/runs/2026-09-14-acars-message-center/design.md as eight numbered sections freezing: the scoping key and FK shape, the DDL, the genericity proof against the four sibling stories, the db module contract, the API contract, the pure module, the client contract, and the verification recipe. The hard questions are listed in the criteria below and each must be answered with a decision and a reason, not deferred to an implementer. No application code is written in this task.
acceptance_criteria: Section 1 freezes the scoping key. It states, citing src/db/schema.ts:12-31 and src/flightManager.ts:236-261 (startFlight inserts the flights row only when the flight begins), whether flight_id is NOT NULL or nullable, its ON DELETE behaviour, and what happens to a message posted when flightManager.appState.currentFlightId is null. If the answer is that a pre-departure PDC or dispatch message needs a planned-leg reference too (acars_pdc_request.md and acars_dispatch_loadsheet.md are both leg-scoped and pre-pushback), section 1 says so and the column ships in section 2 THIS run — adding it later is exactly the migration AC4 forbids. flights.id remains the scoping key per the frozen decision; this section may add a reference, never replace it.

Section 2 freezes the DDL verbatim, column by column with a comment per column, in the house style of src/db/schema.ts (CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS inside applySchema's single db.exec block, plus any CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS), and names the exact position in that block it is inserted at and why (planned_legs' comment at src/db/schema.ts:56-58 shows ordering is load-bearing when a REFERENCES is involved). It states explicitly whether `category` and `direction` carry a CHECK constraint or are TEXT validated in src/acars.ts, and defends the choice against AC4 — acars_position_reports.md asks for a category 'oooi' that the message-center story's own five (pdc, wx, freetext, position-report, dispatch) do not include.

Section 2 also decides, each with one sentence of reason, whether these columns ship now or are deliberately refused: a self-referencing correlation column for request/reply pairs (acars_weather_request.md and acars_dispatch_loadsheet.md are both request→reply), a dedup/idempotency key (acars_pdc_request.md AC2: requesting twice returns an identical clearance), a structured payload column (loadsheet fixed fields; position lat/lon/alt), a read/unread column, and the timestamp column's type and meaning (real time vs sim time) plus the tiebreak used when two rows share a timestamp.

Section 3 is the genericity proof: a table with one row per sibling story (acars_pdc_request, acars_weather_request, acars_position_reports, acars_dispatch_loadsheet) mapping each message that story produces onto the frozen columns, with the literal value each column takes. Any story whose needs do not fit is a defect in section 2, to be fixed there rather than noted here. Alongside it, contracts/ holds a JSON sample row per story row, which T-002 inserts verbatim as its AC4 evidence.

Section 4 freezes src/db/acarsMessages.ts: the exported row type and every exported function signature, following the style of src/db/settings.ts and src/db/flights.ts (getDb() from './connection', no cross-domain imports except via the '../db' barrel). It states the list function's sort order and whether listing is paged or unbounded, and it exposes an insert general enough for a future server-side writer (flightManager emitting OOOI) even though nothing calls it that way this run.

Section 5 freezes the API: method and path for listing a flight's thread and for posting a canned message, the exact request and response JSON for each, the status code and body for every rejection (unknown flight id, non-integer id, malformed body, body not in the canned set, direction/category not permitted from the client), and whether the canned set reaches the client as a third endpoint or as a hand-mirrored client constant — with the reason, given the MCDU client in the other repo will want the same list. It also states the sort order the list endpoint returns in and where 'newest first' is applied (API or client), reconciling AC2's 'chronological' with the story's 'newest at top'.

Section 6 freezes src/acars.ts: every export (the canned set and its ids, the direction/category validators, any body normalisation such as uppercasing or length cap), its purity guarantee (no ./db, no express, no fs, no http/https import), and the list of cases tests/acars.test.ts must cover.

Section 7 freezes the client contract: that the page is client/src/pages/AcarsMessages.tsx at route /flight/:id/acars with an entry point on FlightDetail.tsx, the types added to client/src/types.ts (hand-mirrored from src/types.ts per the note at client/src/types.ts:1-4), how direction and category are made visibly distinguishable (the concrete class names and what they render as, reusing client/src/index.css conventions such as .badge), the render order, the no-reload update path after a successful send, and every state: loading, empty thread, send in flight, send rejected, flight not found, 401.

Section 8 is the verification recipe an implementer follows literally: how to build a scratch cwd from a copy of flights.db plus -wal and -shm, start PORT=3100 recording the PID, create a session (set-password then login) so the requireAuth gate at src/server.ts:79 can be satisfied by curl, exercise every endpoint, prove restart persistence, and stop the server by that recorded PID — never by name or pattern. It also lists, by file and line range, the surfaces that must not change (the applySchema migration block src/db/schema.ts:248-297, the existing /api mount order src/server.ts:117-149, FlightDetail.tsx's existing sections).

Every heading is of the form '## <n>. <title>'. Run .claude/tools/ctx.sh design 2026-09-14-acars-message-center <n> for each of 1 through 8 and paste the first line of each result, so the section numbers are proven sliceable before any envelope cites them.
